answer: Admission needs a quorum from clusters the operator does not control. The spiral is a registry winding identities that share a funder, host or code fingerprint onto one arm. A raven, one claimed identity, takes the k-th slot on its arm only after collecting k lagoons, one-per-epoch vouchers bonded at 30 credits. Each lagoon must come from a different arm that has never vouched for that arm before. So 100 clones must buy 5,050 lagoons from 5,050 unrelated arms, risking 151,500 credits. Colluding arms, or clones that slip the spiral's clustering, break it.
